items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: and he'd say, 'Keepnews All right Wilbur, you got a record date tomorrow -- where's your fiddle?'

ctx.x: the first two cats I run in to -- jamming with -- was Matthew Bee Gene and Ernie Henry, and Matthew just made a record date for Riverside Records, which was a small company; they had a little storefront office on 49th -- between 9th and 10th or something like that. And, he had only did one side, so he said, 'I want you to make the other side.'

So, I made the other side with him, and that was Grauer and Orrin Keepnews my introduction to Bill, (inaudible). And I met some people from the Music Minus One, another storefront operation, and I made a recording -- Music Minus One. See, but when you made those recordings -- you might make it today, but it might take you anywhere from 2 to 4 weeks to get your money.
